claims.text: Donald Trump posted on Truth Social on Saturday that he cancelled planned military strikes against Iran.
Donald Trump stated that the cancellation of US strikes on Iran was contingent on rapidly reaching a deal regarding its nuclear programme and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian news agency Mehr stated on Sunday that Donald Trump's assertion that Tehran requested a pause on strikes was a lie.
Iran's acting defence minister Majid Ebn-e-Reza stated on X that Iranian forces would remain on alert and would not be taken by surprise.
Hassan Ghashghavi, spokesperson for the Iranian parliament's national security commission, stated that mediators were attempting to revive a June agreement brokered by Pakistan.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke with Donald Trump by phone on Saturday to urge de-escalation regarding Iran.
Israeli airstrikes on Gaza on Sunday killed at least 18 Palestinians across Gaza City, Deir al-Balah, and Khan Younis.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi posted on Telegram that negotiations between Tehran and Muscat over the Strait of Hormuz are entering their final stages.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei stated that Iran and Oman were close to an understanding on a new maritime route through the Strait of Hormuz.
On February 28, the US and Israel launched strikes aimed at destroying Iran's missile programme.
Approximately 20 percent of global oil consumption normally passes through the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian posted on X that a memorandum of understanding with the US would become the cornerstone of Tehran's foreign relations.
Maritime trade tracking firm Kpler reported on Friday that vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz had dropped sharply.
Channel 12 reported that Israeli officials and US Central Command first learned of Donald Trump's decision to call off strikes on Iran via his Truth Social post.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi informed Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan that any military attacks by the US or Israel would be met with a proportionate response.
A Danish pilot and a Greek fire service liaison officer were killed when two leased Bell helicopters collided mid-air in Greece while fighting wildfires on Sunday.
A British pilot and a Greek coordinator survived the mid-air helicopter collision near the Attica-Boeotia border.
All Bell helicopters across Greece were grounded following the fatal mid-air collision on Sunday.
Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis expressed his deepest sorrow on X over the loss of the Greek coordinator and Danish pilot.
More than 500 firefighters in Greece fought blazes over 72 hours across areas including Porto Germeno, Psatha, Fokida, Megara, and Kefalonia.
The two firefighting helicopters involved in the collision were leased from Australia's McDermott Aviation.
More than 100 homes were destroyed overnight in wildfires surrounding the coastal village of Porto Germeno, approximately 45 miles northwest of Athens.
Three Greek firefighters died last week from injuries sustained while battling wildfires.
In France, a mega-fire in Gironde was contained after forcing the evacuation of 224,000 people.
The helicopter collision occurred during water-dropping operations near Psatha in western Attica.
A new wildfire broke out overnight on the Ionian island of Kefalonia, prompting evacuations in the Pastra area.
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin described Saturday's bomb blast at a restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square as a brutal terrorist act.
Russian state media reported that the explosion killed a security guard, a restaurant guest, and the female bomber.
The National Anti-Terrorism Committee stated that at least 21 people were injured in the Kudrinskaya Square restaurant explosion.
The explosion took place around 20:00 local time on Saturday at an Italian restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square in central Moscow.
Sergey Goncharov, a veteran of Russia's Alpha counter-terrorism unit, suggested the female carrier might have been an unwitting courier delivered money to carry the package.
REN TV reported that two hospitalized victims succumbed to their wounds on Sunday, raising the unconfirmed death toll to five.
The blast occurred at the entrance of the Balzi Rossi restaurant, located inside a Stalin-era skyscraper on Kudrinskaya Square.
A Ukrainian drone attack on an apartment block in Engels, Russia, killed two people over the weekend.
Russia's Defense Ministry stated that Ukrainian drones struck a Wildberries warehouse in the Samara Oblast.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to be relentless in tackling small boat Channel crossings following the migrant crisis in Ceuta.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez assured Andy Burnham that roughly 98% of the estimated 50,000 migrants who entered Ceuta had been returned to Morocco.
At least 72 people died attempting to cross into Ceuta, with victims drowning or being crushed near the border fence.
Spanish police installed a 500-metre floating barrier off Ceuta's border with Morocco on Saturday.
Around 60,000 migrants surged across the border from Morocco into Spain's enclave of Ceuta over several days starting Thursday.
Morocco's Interior Ministry reported 11 deaths among migrants, mostly from drowning while attempting to cross.
Ceuta leader Juan Jesus Vivas stated that the city's morgue received 88 corpses, including victims from earlier crossing attempts.
Far-right European Parliament member Alvise Pérez was confronted by counterprotesters in Ceuta on Saturday and forced to shelter inside a bar until police intervened.
Vox party leader Santiago Abascal visited Ceuta on Sunday and criticized the Spanish government, labeling the migrant influx an invasion.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni suspended Italy's Schengen agreement with Spain, citing security concerns.
A suicide attack outside a police station in Kabal, Swat district, killed at least 14 people and injured more than two dozen on Sunday.
District police chief Omar Khan stated that demonstrators in Kabal were chanting anti-militant slogans near a police station when the bomber detonated explosives.
Authorities confirmed nine civilians and five police officers were among those killed in the Kabal suicide bombing.
Military spokesperson Ahmad Sharif Chaudhry stated Pakistan recorded 3,145 terrorism-related incidents since January, resulting in 819 security and civilian deaths.
Swat Deputy Inspector General of Police Fida Hussain reported that at least 22 people were wounded in the Kabal attack.
An ambush using explosive-laden drones killed 11 police officers at a checkpoint in Hangu district three days prior to the Kabal bombing.
The Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies recorded 154 terrorism-related deaths across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in July.
The demonstrators in Kabal had assembled for the Olasi Pasoon peace gathering to demand an end to militant violence in Swat Valley.
Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan confirmed that eight people died, eight were missing, and 13 were injured following heavy monsoon rains and landslides.
The India Meteorological Department issued an orange alert for 12 districts in Kerala on Sunday, warning of potential flash floods and mudslides.
Peerumade and Thodupuzha taluks in Idukki received over 200 mm of rainfall on Saturday morning, triggering multiple landslides.
The Kerala State Disaster Management Authority recorded the highest rainfall of 320 mm at Ayyankunnu in Kannur district on Saturday.
Educational institutions in Pathanamthitta, Wayanad, Kannur, and Kasaragod districts were declared closed on August 3 due to severe weather.
Three-year-old Abdul Muhaini and four-year-old Adam Ayman drowned after falling into a swollen stream in Malappuram.
In Gujarat's Vadodara district, rescue teams evacuated around 150 people, including 140 students, from a flooded hostel near Waghodia.
A man hurled a slipper at Independent MP Pappu Yadav during a press conference at his Delhi residence on Sunday evening around 6:15 p.m.
Delhi police took into custody a man identified as Sumit from Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh, for throwing the slipper at Pappu Yadav.
Pappu Yadav stated he was addressing questions regarding missing gold and silver following a skit on Ram Temple donation theft staged in Parliament on July 31.
Varanasi police registered an FIR against Pappu Yadav, Rahul Gandhi, and Awadhesh Prasad following complaints by seers regarding the Ram Temple donation skit.
Police questioned a man named Sumit, a 34-year-old iron fabrication business owner from Ghaziabad, following the footwear attack.
Congress media head Pawan Khera criticized Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and the force for failing to protect Pappu Yadav at his residence.
Pappu Yadav's media convenor alleged that an attacker drew a knife during the altercation at the press conference.
Hundreds of students staged an indefinite sit-in at Jaipal Singh Munda stadium in Ranchi for a fifth consecutive day on Sunday to protest competitive exam irregularities.
Protesting students conducted a torchlight procession from Jaipal Singh Munda stadium to Albert Ekka Chowk in Ranchi on Sunday evening.
Protesters demanded a CBI probe into all recruitment exams held by JPSC and JSSC over the last seven years and the cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Preliminary Test held on April 19.
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke posted on X extending support to the students protesting in Jharkhand.
A 25-year-old man named Heeralal climbed a 100-foot mobile tower at Jaipal Singh Munda stadium on Sunday morning before being rescued by police.
The BJYM and BJP held demonstrations across East Singhbhum, West Singhbhum, and Chatra demanding a CBI investigation into JPSC and JSSC exam irregularities.
Karnataka began releasing Cauvery water from Kabini Dam on Saturday, raising discharge from 500 cusecs to 25,000 cusecs by Saturday night.
The water level at Mettur Dam stood at 73.33 feet against its full capacity of 120 feet on Sunday.
Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar stated that Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay agreed to postpone his planned visit to Bengaluru regarding the Cauvery dispute.
The Cauvery Water Management Authority directed Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days.
D.K. Shivakumar stated that Karnataka had received only about 35 percent of its normal rainfall so far this year.
Kannada Chaluvali leader Vatal Nagaraj stated that a proposed state-wide bandh in Karnataka will proceed on August 13 despite government appeals to withdraw it.
BJP Tamil Nadu president Nainar Nagenthran accused the Congress party of cheating Tamil Nadu farmers whenever it comes to power in Karnataka.
